learn.title: What is a variable?
learn.body: A variable is a name that holds a value. Think of a labelled box: the label is the name, and what is inside is the value. You make one with `=`, which means store, not equals.

learn.title: Making a variable
learn.body: This prints 12, then 13. The second `=` replaces the old value. A variable can change, which is why it is called a variable.

learn.title: Choosing names
learn.body: Names can use letters, digits and underscores, but cannot start with a digit or contain spaces. `player_name` is fine; `2nd` is not. Python is case sensitive: `Age` and `age` are two different names.
Pick names that say what the value means. `price` is easier to read than `p`.

questions.explanation: The second line replaces the first value, so `x` is 9.

questions.prompt: `n = 3`, then `n = n + 4`, then `print(n)`. What is printed?
questions.explanation: `n + 4` is 3 + 4 = 7, and 7 is stored back in `n`.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid variable name?
questions.explanation: Only `my_score` uses letters and an underscore. The others start with a digit, contain a space or contain a minus sign.

questions.prompt: In Python, `=` is used to \_\_ a value in a name.
questions.explanation: `=` stores a value. Comparing uses `==`, which comes later.

questions.prompt: Match each line to what it does.
questions.explanation: `=` stores, `print` shows, and `age + 1` is worked out before it is stored.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so the program prints 10.
questions.explanation: A variable must exist before you use it: `a` first, then `b` from `a`, then print.
